speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; could you tell me exactly where the pain starts and how far down it travels? On a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the pain right now? Do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that leg or your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the sudden onset after exercise and radiation into the foot, are you currently experiencing any noticeable weakness in your leg or foot, and have you noticed any changes in bowel or bladder control? Also, does the pain worsen when you cough or sneeze?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation.

The clinical picture of sudden onset back pain during exercise, radiating to the foot, and worsening with movement is classic for a herniated disc pressing on a nerve root. I am confident in this diagnosis based on your symptoms and do not require further testing or questions at this time.
